_comment: John Doe's verified claims (fictional). Every resume line must trace to at least one of these. 'facts' lists what a line may state: figures, systems and phrases. A line that states a figure or a system not in any claim it matches is blocked. Optional per claim: 'voice' is written (the default: on the page and aloud), spoken (aloud only, never printed) or interview (aloud, and only when asked: an intro that volunteers it warns); 'patterns' are case-insensitive regexes that recognise the claim in prose (a spoken or interview claim needs them); 'requires' is a regex the same sentence must also match when the claim is said, such as the word that keeps an estimate an estimate. In JSON a word boundary is written \\b: \b is a backspace, and claimcheck refuses it. 'titles_not_held' lists titles he must never be presented as holding (matched title-cased, case-sensitive). See docs/INTERVIEW_PREP.md.

claims.text: Product owner for the company's NetSuite ERP, covering order-to-cash and procure-to-pay.
Led the rollout of Coupa procurement to 3 business units and 420 requesters.
Ran the month-end close improvement program; close shortened from 9 working days to 6.
Prioritized the backlog for the finance systems team and chaired its weekly intake meeting.
Built SQL and Excel reporting for finance leadership.
Coordinated user acceptance testing and release sign-off for quarterly ERP releases.
4.5 years at Northwind Traders, 2021 to present.
Rolled Coupa out one business unit at a time, with requester training before each go-live and a cutover checklist he owned.
facts: one business unit at a time

claims.text: Mapped every month-end close task with the accounting team and moved the bank reconciliations and accrual entries into NetSuite saved searches; a daily close stand-up replaced the end-of-month status email.
Introduced a scoring rubric at the weekly intake meeting: every request is ranked on value, effort and risk, and the ranked list is shared with requesters.
The shorter close freed an estimated 120 analyst hours a month. It is his estimate from the accounting team's timesheets, so it is said aloud with its qualifier and never printed.
At intake he turned down a regional request for a custom Coupa approval workflow, showed the region that the standard approval flow already covered its case, and the region adopted the standard flow.

The Coupa cutover for the third business unit was rolled back after 2 days because its supplier records had not been cleaned, a step his cutover checklist did not have. He ran the cleanup of 1,800 duplicate supplier records, added a supplier-data check to the checklist, and the unit went live 5 weeks later.
